headline: ASX fell 0.75% today as RBA rate hike fears bite, while the US-Iran conflict shows signs of easing and Microsoft's big earnings drop Tuesday night AEST.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI had a rough session today, falling 2.15% alongside the broader ASX tech selloff. No specific catalyst — this one tracks global AI stocks and tends to move with overall market sentiment. The long-term AI growth story remains intact.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS slipped another 2.13% today, continuing its weak run. Lithium prices remain depressed globally as EV demand growth has come in softer than expected. This is a structural headwind, not just a one-day blip — the stock is now down nearly 39% from your entry.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE fell 1.32% today. Emerging market ETFs have been under pressure as the stronger US dollar and ongoing geopolitical uncertainty — including the Iran situation — weigh on investor appetite for riskier assets.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG dipped 0.71% today, tracking a soft ASX session. As a diversified fund holding a broad mix of global and Australian shares, it tends to mirror overall market mood — nothing specific to worry about here.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS edged down 0.51% today. This reflects a slight lag in the AUD-priced version of US equities — the underlying US market was flat last night, so this dip is mostly AUD/currency noise rather than a signal about US stocks.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: TTWO nudged up 0.61% last night, buoyed by ongoing GTA 6 hype — a third trailer is widely anticipated and Take-Two has been actively fighting AI-generated fake leaks, suggesting launch preparations are well underway.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: GOOG crept up 0.24% last night after reporting mixed earnings — cloud revenue surged strongly but other segments came in below some analyst expectations. The market is broadly comfortable with the result, with the cloud growth story keeping sentiment positive.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: MSFT was essentially flat last night, up just 0.03%, as investors hold their breath ahead of Q4 earnings on July 29 (Tuesday night AEST). Expectations are high — analysts are bullish on Azure cloud and AI growth — so the print will be a big moment for this holding.

watch_today.title: Microsoft earnings Tuesday night — big moment for your MSFT holding
watch_today.detail: MSFT reports Q4 earnings on July 29 US time — that's Wednesday morning AEST. The stock is rated Strong Buy by multiple analysts on the back of Azure cloud and AI growth. Your position is currently down about 14% from your entry, so a strong result could be a meaningful recovery catalyst. Hold tight and watch the print.

watch_today.title: PLS continues to slide — down 38.6% from your entry
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals fell another 2.13% today and is now one of your biggest losses in dollar terms (-$57.86 AUD). The lithium market remains structurally oversupplied and there's no near-term catalyst on the horizon. For a long-term holder, the question is whether you still believe in lithium's role in the EV transition — if yes, sit tight. If your conviction has changed, it's worth reassessing your thesis, not just reacting to the price.

watch_today.title: GXAI down 18% from entry — AI theme intact long-term
watch_today.detail: The Global X AI ETF dropped 2.15% today and is your second-largest loss at -$53.89. However, this week brought fresh signals that the AI investment boom is alive — Microsoft launched a new MAI model family and both MSFT and Nvidia are lobbying hard on AI policy. The long-term thesis for AI stocks looks solid. Sit tight.

watch_today.title: RBA rate decision looming — watch inflation data this week
watch_today.detail: Key Australian inflation data drops this week, followed by RBA Governor Michele Bullock's speech. Markets are split on whether the RBA hikes rates next month. A hike would likely push ASX lower and squeeze households further. Your VDHG and VGE holdings would feel short-term pressure, but for a long-term holder, any dip from a rate decision is noise.

watch_today.title: GOOG mixed earnings — cloud surges, long-term case intact
watch_today.detail: Alphabet reported mixed Q4 earnings last night — cloud revenue surged strongly, which is the key long-term driver, but some other segments were softer. The stock edged up 0.24% on the result. Your position is up 3.79% overall. The cloud and AI story remains compelling — hold and let it run.

watch_today.title: Oil dropped sharply — good news for Australian consumers
watch_today.detail: Crude oil (WTI) fell 3.12% last night to $89.31/barrel, easing from recent highs driven by Middle East tensions. This should take some pressure off petrol prices, which had been threatening to push above $2/litre. Good background news for household budgets and consumer-facing stocks.

world.summary: The US-Iran conflict appears to be pausing at a critical juncture, Brazil is pushing back against US election interference, and Trump's mail-in voting executive order has been blocked by the courts.

stories.title: US-Iran conflict enters an uneasy pause as Trump holds off on escalation
stories.why_it_matters: Trump has decided against a major new military escalation against Iran, with advisers raising concerns about the cost and risks of going further. Trump claimed the US has 'hit Iran very hard' and crippled it, but both sides appear to be stepping back from the brink — at least for now. The Houthi militia backed by Iran also fired missiles at Saudi Arabia this weekend, keeping regional tensions alive. For everyday Australians, this matters because ongoing conflict in the Middle East drives oil prices and global uncertainty — the pause has already helped push crude down over 3% last night.

stories.title: Brazil blocks US diplomats over election interference fears
stories.why_it_matters: Brazil has refused to grant visas to a US government delegation that Brazilian officials say was planning to meddle in their upcoming elections. It's a significant diplomatic rebuff — Brazil is essentially accusing the US of trying to undermine its democratic process. This adds to growing global friction over US foreign policy under Trump and signals that South American nations are increasingly willing to publicly push back on Washington.

stories.title: US appeals court blocks Trump's executive order restricting mail-in voting
stories.why_it_matters: A US federal appeals court has ruled that Trump cannot implement his executive order aimed at restricting mail-in voting across 23 states. The order would have required voters to provide proof of citizenship and limited how ballots could be returned. Courts have now blocked it, delivering a significant legal defeat for the Trump administration's push to reshape how Americans vote. This is part of a broader pattern of the courts acting as a check on executive power in the current US political environment.

stories.title: Trump administration admits cancelling clean energy grants to Democratic-led states
stories.why_it_matters: The Trump White House has officially admitted it cancelled billions of dollars in clean energy grants specifically targeting states that vote Democrat. Officials confirmed the grants were pulled as part of a politically motivated rollback of Biden-era climate spending. This is significant because it confirms what critics had alleged — that federal funding is being used as a political weapon — and it sets up major legal battles over whether the executive branch can unilaterally cancel congressionally approved spending.

stories.title: Houthi militia fires missiles at Saudi Arabia as Middle East tensions persist
stories.why_it_matters: Yemen's Houthi rebels, backed by Iran, have claimed responsibility for a fresh missile attack on Saudi Arabia, escalating regional tensions even as the US and Iran appear to be stepping back from direct confrontation. The Houthis have been emboldened throughout the US-Iran conflict and show no signs of standing down. Ongoing Houthi attacks threaten shipping in the Red Sea, which affects global trade routes and can push up the cost of goods worldwide.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 fell 0.75% today, dragged down by rate hike fears and cautious sentiment ahead of key US earnings. Last night the S&P 500 was virtually flat (+0.05%) while the NASDAQ slipped 0.64%. Oil fell sharply, gold hit new highs, and the Aussie dollar ticked up slightly.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Fell today as RBA rate hike fears weighed on sentiment, particularly on property and consumer stocks.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Essentially flat last night — markets in holding pattern ahead of a big week of US tech earnings.

indicators.name: NASDAQ
indicators.note: Slipped last night despite mixed-but-OK results from Alphabet. Tech investors appear cautious ahead of Microsoft's earnings.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Fell sharply last night as the US-Iran conflict showed signs of easing, reducing fears of a supply disruption.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold nudged to another record high as investors seek safe havens amid ongoing geopolitical uncertainty.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar ticked up slightly — still just below 70 US cents. A stronger AUD slightly reduces the AUD value of your US holdings.

politics.summary: The RBA rate decision is looming large this week, with Australians facing a potential double hit of higher interest rates and petrol prices pushing toward $2/litre. Meanwhile, Albanese finds himself at odds with his own party's policy on voluntary assisted dying consultations.

stories.title: RBA rate hike next month could force thousands of homeowners to sell
stories.why_it_matters: A staggering number of Australian mortgage holders are already in stress, and a rate hike next month from the RBA (Reserve Bank of Australia) could push some over the edge and force property sales. Key inflation data drops this week, which will shape whether the RBA pulls the trigger in August. At the same time, petrol prices are threatening to push above $2 a litre, squeezing household budgets from two directions. If you own property or are watching the housing market, this week's data is crucial.

stories.title: Critics accuse RBA of 'wanting people to lose their jobs' to fight inflation
stories.why_it_matters: The RBA's strategy of raising interest rates to crush inflation works by slowing the economy — which means fewer jobs and less consumer spending. Critics argue the Bank is being too aggressive and essentially engineering unemployment to hit its inflation target. RBA Governor Michele Bullock is speaking this week, and her tone will be closely watched by markets. A hawkish (tough on rates) tone could push the ASX lower and increase mortgage pain for millions of Australians.

stories.title: Albanese at odds with Labor over telehealth for euthanasia consultations
stories.why_it_matters: Labor's own party policy now supports allowing telehealth (online/phone medical consultations) to be used for voluntary assisted dying (VAD) consultations, but Prime Minister Albanese has publicly distanced himself from this position. It creates an awkward split within the government — Labor's platform says one thing, the PM says another. VAD is already legal in all Australian states, but access via telehealth would make it easier for people in rural and remote areas to access the service. The policy tension is likely to grow.

ai.summary: Microsoft launched a new family of AI models this week, the AI regulatory debate is heating up globally, and Google's much-anticipated Gemini 3.5 Pro is still nowhere to be seen.

stories.title: Microsoft launches MAI — a new family of AI models for reasoning, voice, coding and images
stories.why_it_matters: Microsoft has unveiled a new suite of AI models called MAI, designed to handle a range of tasks — reasoning through complex problems, generating images, understanding voice, and writing code. This is Microsoft building its own AI layer on top of its partnership with OpenAI, giving it more independence and flexibility. For your MSFT holding, this matters: it shows Microsoft is not just reselling OpenAI's tech but building its own AI stack, which strengthens its long-term competitive position heading into Tuesday's earnings.

stories.title: Microsoft and Nvidia lobby US government to oppose 'open AI' regulation
stories.why_it_matters: Microsoft and Nvidia are pushing the US government to block regulations that would require AI companies to make their models open-source (freely available for anyone to use or copy). Their argument is that 'open AI' rules would hand an advantage to Chinese rivals who could take the technology and run with it without the same safety guardrails. This is a significant lobbying fight that will shape how AI is regulated globally — and it directly affects how companies like MSFT and Google can monetise and protect their AI investments.

stories.title: Where is Google's Gemini 3.5 Pro? Announced months ago, still not released
stories.why_it_matters: Google announced Gemini 3.5 Pro — its next flagship AI model — at Google I/O earlier this year, but it still hasn't been released. That's months of radio silence, raising questions about whether Google is running into technical problems or is holding back to time a launch strategically. Meanwhile, OpenAI released GPT-5.5 and Anthropic has Claude Opus 4.7 on the market. Google falling behind on its own announced timeline is worth watching for GOOG holders — the AI race moves fast and the competition is not standing still.

stories.title: OpenAI GPT-5.5 vs Claude Opus 4.7 — the AI model battle is heating up
stories.why_it_matters: OpenAI's newest model GPT-5.5 and Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.7 are now being directly compared — and the competition between the two is fierce. Both models are pushing the boundaries of what AI can reason through and write. This matters to everyday users because the AI tools you use for work, writing, and research are getting dramatically better every few months. It also matters for investors: the AI infrastructure boom (cloud, chips, data centres) is being driven by exactly this kind of model competition.

sport.summary: A big NRL weekend with the Titans demolishing the Dragons, the Bulldogs thumping the Warriors, and the Cowboys downing the Broncos. The AFL had Brisbane Lions and Geelong in action. Plus injury news from the Knights.

stories.title: Gold Coast Titans destroy St George Dragons 38–18 in Sunday clash
stories.why_it_matters: Your Gold Coast Titans put on a dominant performance at St George Venues Jubilee Stadium today, winning 38–18. A massive result for local Gold Coast fans — the Titans look in strong form heading into the back half of the season.

stories.title: Bulldogs thump Warriors 18–6 in statement win, Warriors suffer injury blow
stories.why_it_matters: The Canterbury Bulldogs were dominant in their 18–6 win over the Warriors on Saturday. The Warriors suffered significant injury pain in the loss — adding to their growing injury list and dealing a blow to their finals hopes. The Bulldogs meanwhile look like genuine premiership contenders.

stories.title: Cowboys beat Broncos 18–10 — Brisbane's season on life support
stories.why_it_matters: North Queensland Cowboys beat the Brisbane Broncos 18–10 on Saturday night, leaving the Broncos' season described as 'on life support'. Brisbane have now lost consecutive games in crucial circumstances — their run to the finals is looking increasingly dire. For Queensland footy fans, the Cowboys are looking dangerous while the Broncos are fading fast.

stories.title: Knights suffer double injury blow — $13m man goes down
stories.why_it_matters: The Newcastle Knights suffered a painful week with a double injury blow — their high-paid marquee player and another key squad member both going down. The Knights narrowly lost to the Roosters 23–22 on Friday night, and the injury news makes their path through the second half of the season even harder. Details on the specific players and recovery times to be confirmed, but the club is in damage control mode.

stories.title: Brisbane Lions down Port Adelaide in late avalanche to stay in top-two hunt
stories.why_it_matters: The Brisbane Lions came from behind with a late scoring avalanche to beat Port Adelaide on Sunday, keeping themselves in the hunt for a top-two finish on the AFL ladder. A top-two finish means a double chance in the finals — a significant prize this late in the season. Brisbane look like genuine flag contenders heading into the business end of 2026.
